Brookfield is bookended by two lakes: Candlewood Lake, the largest lake in Connecticut, runs along the west side, and Lake Lillinonah runs along the east.

Five local staples:
1. Candlewood Lake and the Brookfield Town Beach
2. Lake Lillinonah, a long, narrow dammed section of the Housatonic
3. Still River Greenway: about 2.25 paved, car-free miles from the Municipal Center to the Four Corners town center
4. Brookfield Craft Center, in the old grist mill on the falls of the Still River
5. Four Corners and Federal Road for shops and dining

Up to $25,000 toward your first home, at 0% with no monthly payment.

Connecticut's Time To Own program is a forgivable second loan for down payment and closing costs, run by CHFA. If your household income is at or below 80% of area median, you can get up to $25,000. Between 80% and 100%, up to $18,750.

For Danbury and the rest of the Western CT region, CHFA's current limits (June 2026) are $156,800 for 100% of median and $125,440 for 80%.

The fine print: it only pairs with a CHFA first mortgage from a participating lender, the minimum is $3,000, and state funding is limited. Get pre-approved for both before you make offers.

Text:
A full house on Thursday is the hardest day of the year on a septic system. The EPA says many septic failures happen during the holiday season.

Most homes in Newtown, Sandy Hook, Southbury and the rest of our area run on a well and septic, so here are five checks before the guests arrive:
1. Turkey grease goes in a can, not down the drain.
2. Space out the dishwasher and laundry.
3. Keep guest cars off the leach field.
4. Only toilet paper gets flushed.
5. Know when your tank was last pumped (EPA: about every 3 to 5 years).

And thank you. Four years and 21 homes closed across Western CT. I'm grateful to every client who trusted me with their move. Happy Thanksgiving.

Wilton packs a national park, a pond beach, a 200-year-old farm and a train to Grand Central into one town.

1. Weir Farm: Connecticut's only national park dedicated to American painting, with free ranger-led tours.
2. Merwin Meadows: a 17-acre park in Wilton Center with a pond beach in summer.
3. Woodcock Nature Center: about 150 acres on the Ridgefield line, with boardwalks over the wetlands.
4. Ambler Farm: town-owned, about 200 years old, open dawn to dusk every day.
5. Metro-North: stations in Wilton Center and Cannondale, about 1 hour 35 minutes to Grand Central.
